note: Clean pass, PARTIAL verification. SOURCE: Gordils J, Elliot AJ, Jamieson JP, Zhang Y (2021) PLoS ONE 16(1):e0245671, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0245671, CC BY 4.0. Item wording is verbatim from S1 Appendix (s001, DOCX), section 'Perceived Interracial Trust', which prints the four sentences and the anchor line 'Seven-point scale (1 = "Not at all"; 4 = "Somewhat"; 7 = "Completely")'; the paper's Methods repeats the same anchors for this scale ('1 = not at all, 7 = completely') and quotes the second sentence as its example item. MAPPING (paper_order): the IRW codes TRUST1..TRUST4 ARE the source spreadsheets' own column names -- data/gordils_2021_interracial.py melts df[['id'] + ['TRUST1'..'TRUST4']] with no rename and no positional step -- but the appendix lists its four sentences UNNUMBERED, so the assignment of sentence k to TRUSTk is inferred from presentation order. LEVEL-1 SOURCES WERE CHECKED AND HAVE NO ITEM TEXT: S1 Data (s004.xlsx) and S4 Data (s007.xlsx) carry bare column headers only, and the three SPSS syntax files (s005/s006/s008) contain no VARIABLE LABELS or VALUE LABELS for any TRUST variable (their only label statements are for filter_$). VERIFIED, decisively, on the option_text<->resp axis: the S3 Data syntax defines MISTRUST = MEAN(8-TRUST1, 8-TRUST2, 8-TRUST3, 8-TRUST4), i.e. the live table stores TRUST in the trust direction, and recomputing the paper's Study 1 test on that composite reproduces it exactly -- t(845) = 3.318 vs published 3.32, 95% CI [0.14, 0.53] vs published [0.14, 0.53], d = 0.228 vs published 0.23, M(HRC) 3.527 vs M(LRC) 3.192. Under flipped anchors the same test gives -0.335, the wrong sign. That also settles Step 3b: these four columns are the paper's interracial-mistrust scale, not another instrument from the same battery. NOT VERIFIED: which appendix sentence is TRUST1 vs TRUST2 vs TRUST3 vs TRUST4. No route exists -- all four items share one 1-7 scale (route 2 out), the scale is a single unidimensional block with no published subscale split (routes 3, 5 out), it has no reverse-worded item (route 6), no marker item (route 7), the paper publishes no per-item statistics (route 1), the item text implies no parameter (route 4), and the source stores integers rather than labels (route 9). Route 8 was attempted and is not decisive: pooled per-item means are TRUST1 4.560, TRUST2 4.325, TRUST3 4.534, TRUST4 4.348, which does group positions {1,3} above {2,4} as the appendix order's character items ('basically honest', 'basically good and kind') vs its explicit-trust items ('trustworthy', 'trustful'), but that reading is post-hoc, a random pairing matches it 1 time in 3, and it separates no item from its partner; it is NOT counted as evidence. The correlation matrix offers nothing either -- r(2,3)=0.870, r(2,4)=0.877, r(3,4)=0.879 are indistinguishable and only TRUST1 stands slightly apart (0.768-0.799), with no pre-specifiable reason it should. TRANSCRIPTION: verbatim, no normalisation. instructions carries the appendix's own framing sentence for this scale ('Respondents were asked to give a score ranging from 1 to 7, where 1 represented very low trust in others and 7 very high trust.') -- note it is the appendix's third-person description, not a participant-facing imperative like the sibling avoidance and discrimination scales have, because the appendix prints none for this scale. The appendix gives TWO anchor descriptions for this scale (that sentence, and the 'Not at all / Somewhat / Completely' line); option_text ships the second because the paper's Methods states it explicitly for the mistrust measure, and the first is preserved in instructions rather than dropped. resp 2, 3, 5 and 6 are unlabelled in the source and ship blank, not padded. section_prompt and correct_response blank (single-section attitude scale, no key). RIGHTS: no restriction found to quote. The deposit and the article are CC BY 4.0; the parent instrument is Yamagishi & Yamagishi's (1994) General Trust Scale, published in Motivation and Emotion with no fee and no redistribution clause locatable, and IRW's copy comes from the CC BY appendix in any case. Neither 2026-09-04 trigger fires. SIBLINGS: gordils_2021_discrimination and gordils_2021_behavioral_avoidance shipped in batch_041 from the same S1 Appendix and the same paper_order basis; conventions (instrument naming, single trivial section_id, blank unlabelled anchors) follow them.
public_note: The four items are stored in the TRUST direction (higher = more trust, 1 = 'Not at all' to 7 = 'Completely'), whereas the paper's own analyses use the reverse-scored composite MISTRUST = mean(8 - TRUST1..4); recomputing that composite from these columns reproduces the published Study 1 effect exactly, t(845) = 3.318 against a published 3.32. The study's appendix also prints two different anchor descriptions for this scale, and the response labels shipped here are the one the paper's Methods section states (1 = not at all, 7 = completely).
